def: A model that reads the query and a document together as one input and outputs a single relevance score for that pair.
A second-stage model that reorders the shortlist returned by a cheap first-stage retriever to put the best results at the top.
The number of first-stage candidates handed to the reranker, which sets both its cost and the recall ceiling.
The best end-to-end recall a reranked system can reach, equal to the first stage's recall at the rerank depth.
A pipeline where a fast, recall-oriented retriever proposes candidates and a slower, precision-oriented model reorders them.
A non-relevant passage that the first stage ranks highly, used in training so the model learns to reject the mistakes it will actually meet.
Scoring each candidate independently, for example the probability that a model answers yes to 'is this relevant?'.
Asking a model which of two candidates is more relevant and building an order from many such comparisons.
Giving a model a numbered list of candidates and asking it to return them in order of relevance.
Ranking a long candidate list in overlapping windows from the back to the front so strong passages move towards the top.
